Dabur India
The board of directors of Dabur India had declared an interim dividend of ₹3.50 per equity share, with a face value of ₹1 each, for FY27. It also fixed November 10, 2026, as the record date.
The consumer goods company had reported its earnings for the July-September quarter of the 2026-27 financial year (Q2 FY27), in which it saw its consolidated net profit jump 11.7% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹505.50 crore. In the same period last year, the company had logged a profit of ₹452.55 crore.
Its consolidated revenue from operations advanced by 11.6% YoY to ₹3,563.07 crore during the quarter under review, compared with ₹3,191.32 crore in the second quarter of the 2025-26 fiscal year (Q2 FY26).
However, the firm clocked a 13% YoY increase in its material cost to ₹1,822.7 crore in Q2 FY27, in contrast to ₹1,613.5 crore in the year-ago period.

NBCC India
The state-owned company reported a 33.8% YoY increase in net profit to ₹206 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared to ₹154 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from operations rose 16.5% to ₹3,396 crore from ₹2,914 crore.
Its earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) more than doubled to ₹225.5 crore from ₹104.5 crore in the year-ago period. The EBITDA margin improved to 6.6% in Q2 FY27, up from 3.6% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.
CONCOR
Container Corporation of India’s (CONCOR) board of directors declared the company’s second interim dividend of ₹1.90 per equity share, with a face value of ₹5 each, amounting to ₹144.71 crore.
It also fixed Wednesday, November 11, 2026, as the record date for the same, adding that the dividend will be paid on or after Friday, November 20.
The multi-modal logistics solutions provider had reported its earnings for Q2 FY27, posting a 6.8% yearly fall in its consolidated net profit to ₹353 crore. In the corresponding period of the preceding fiscal year, the company had logged a profit of ₹378.70 crore.
The company’s consolidated revenue from operations rose marginally YoY to ₹2,378.57 crore during the quarter under review, as against ₹2,354.53 crore in the second quarter of the 2025-26 fiscal year (Q2 FY26).
